chunks.text: Cardiovascular and neurological disease together impose one of the largest preventable disease burdens in India, yet every application-specific integrated circuit used in the cardiac and neurological monitoring devices sold domestically is currently imported. This paper presents CardioNeural-SoC, an indigenous, mixed-signal System-on-Chip architecture designed to consolidate a 4-channel electrocardiogram (ECG) front-end, a 2-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) front-end, a photoplethysmography (PPG) interface, a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter array, a RISC-V-based digital signal processing core with hardware accelerators for arrhythmia and seizure-onset classification, an AES-128-secured Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE 5.3) interface, and an ultra-low-power management unit onto a single 28 nm CMOS die. chunks.text:
4. System Architecture
CardioNeural-SoC is architected as a fully monolithic mixed-signal chip integrating six major subsystems on a single 28 nm CMOS die, replacing the multi-chip approach used in current Indian-assembled patient monitors. Table 3 summarizes the constituent subsystems, their target specifications, and their individual power budgets; the design targets a total chip power below 2.3 mW in full-active monitoring mode and below 180 µW in duty-cycled wearable mode, with a die-area target below 8 mm² in 28 nm CMOS.
Subsystem Description Key Specification (Target) Node Power Budget (Target)
Cardiac AFE 4-channel biopotential CMRR > 110 dB; gain 40–28 nm
Neural AFE 2-channel EEG front-end Input noise < 50 nV/√Hz; 28 nm
PPG/SpO2 Dual-wavelength photodetector interface 16-bit resolution 28 nm
16-bit ADC 6-channel SAR ADC with noise shaping SNR > 94 dB; 4 kSPS 28 nm
RISC-V DSP 32-bit in-order core + QRS detection; AF 28 nm

chunks.text:
8. Discussion
The principal contribution of this work is architectural and pre-silicon: a verified RTL implementation and a synthesized sub-block (layer1_top) demonstrating that the proposed multi-modal acquisition and on-chip classification architecture is implementable within a digital-logic budget consistent with the system-level power target in Table 3, once duty-cycling is applied. The zero-slack timing closure reported in Section 6.3 and the 46.06 mW worst-case synthesis-stage power figure for layer1_top both warrant continued attention during physical implementation: zero slack at the gate level typically requires either a relaxed clock period, pipeline restructuring, or further logic optimization once net parasitics are introduced at place-and-route, and the energy-accumulator block's power should be evaluated under its intended duty-cycled (rather than continuous) operating profile before being treated as representative of always-on power.

chunks.text:
The contribution of this paper is intentionally scoped to what has been concretely implemented and verified at the time of writing: a system-level architecture spanning six integrated subsystems; full-chip RTL functional verification via a system-level testbench; and gate-level synthesis, timing, power, and area results for the discrete-wavelet-transform (DWT)-based sub-band energy feature extraction block that underlies the on-chip arrhythmia/seizure classification path. Consistent with responsible reporting of pre-silicon work, no fabricated-silicon measurements, clinical validation results, or noise/SNR/CMRR bench measurements are claimed in this paper; these remain explicit objectives of the subsequent tape-out and post-silicon validation phase described in Section 8.
